comment: Overhead electric facilities exist on multiple boundaries of the site. Proposed driveways, parking areas, and retaining walls are located in proximity to overhead lines. comment: Electrical design plan shows underground electrical service infrastructure. Utility plan does not clearly distinguish between primary and secondary overhead electric lines where they cross each other. Documentation of overhead line crossing details is not provided.

applicableAreas: building-mounted and area lighting

comment: Landscape plan shows proposed tree plantings throughout site, including areas in proximity to overhead electric lines on western, northern, and southern boundaries. Compliance with tree species restrictions cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: landscape areas, parking lot trees, street yard trees

comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows meter pad locations. No analysis of obstructions from buildings, fences, walls, or landscaping is provided.
applicableAreas: proposed electric meter locations

comment: Proposed buildings are located near Valley View Road where streetlight poles may exist. No dimension shows clearance distance from building locations to existing streetlight pole locations. Clearance verification is absent.
applicableAreas: if streetlight poles exist adjacent to site

comment: Existing survey (Sheet 4) shows utility poles on and adjacent to property. Potential conflicts with proposed accessible paths, driveways, or site features cannot be verified without complete down guy wire documentation.
applicableAreas: if down guy wires from poles near driveways or accessible paths

comment: Plat sheet (Sheet 2) shows easement boundaries but does not explicitly identify down guy anchor easements. If down guy anchors from poles near the property exist, dedicated 10-foot-wide easements extending 5 feet past ground entry points are required but not documented.
applicableAreas: if down guy anchors exist on property

comment: Sequence of construction is outlined on Sheet 3. Verification that staging areas maintain 10-foot radial clearance from overhead lines cannot be determined.
applicableAreas: construction staging areas

comment: Overhead electric distribution line (OHE) is present on the site. Proposed tree species are listed on Sheet 35 (Cedar Elm, Live Oak, Mexican Redbud, Texas Mountain Laurel), but utility-compatible (UC) status cannot be verified from submitted documents as ECM Appendix F is not included. Additionally, no clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan to verify whether any non-utility-compatible trees are within the required 15-foot lateral distance from the distribution conductor.
applicableAreas: Bottom and east property boundaries where overhead electric distribution line is present

comment: Proposed tree species list does not include mature height specifications. Sheet 35 provides minimum container sizes (100 gal., 45 gal.) and caliper inches (4", 2.5") but not the mature heights required to determine which trees are 'large trees' (40+ feet per ECM Appendix F). Without mature height data and clearance dimensions, compliance with the 25-foot distribution clearance requirement for large trees cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas near the overhead electric distribution line along south and east property boundaries

comment: Utility pole symbols are shown on the landscape plan (Sheet 31) and site plan (Sheet 9) along the OHE line, but their exact locations are not dimensioned. Proposed tree locations are shown but no clearance dimensions are provided from trees to the poles. Therefore, the 10-foot lateral clearance requirement cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas where utility poles are shown along the overhead electric line

comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical infrastructure (transformers, pull boxes, electrical meters) but does not clearly distinguish pad-mounted equipment from other electrical elements. The landscape plan does not show electrical equipment locations in relation to proposed trees. Therefore, compliance with the 10-foot clearance requirement from pad-mounted equipment cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas where pad-mounted electrical equipment may be located

comment: Electrical design plan (Sheet 21) shows underground electrical elements but the landscape plan (Sheet 31) does not overlay electrical equipment locations with proposed tree locations. Clearance dimensions from trees to underground equipment are not shown. The 5-foot lateral clearance requirement cannot be verified from the submitted plans.
applicableAreas: Areas where underground electrical equipment is located near proposed trees

comment: While underground electrical equipment is shown on Sheet 21, the landscape plan does not provide root barrier specifications or details. No clearance dimensions are shown from trees to underground equipment to determine whether any trees fall within the 20-foot threshold requiring root barriers. Root barrier requirements therefore cannot be verified.
applicableAreas: Areas where trees are proposed within 20 lateral feet of underground electrical equipment

comment: The landscape plan (Sheet 31) uses abbreviation codes to label tree locations (M = Mitigation Tree, SY = Street Yard Tree, PL = Parking Lot Tree, P = Parking Buffer Point Tree) but provides no legend on that sheet correlating these codes to the specific botanical names. The plant schedule with species identification is located on a separate sheet (Sheet 35). A reader cannot determine which species is planted at which location on the landscape plan without cross-referencing multiple sheets.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan areas near overhead electric facilities

comment: The landscape plan does not indicate mature heights for any of the proposed trees. Sheet 35 provides minimum container specifications and caliper sizes but does not specify the mature height for any tree species. Without mature height information on or cross-referenced to the landscape plan, large trees (those with mature height 40+ feet per ECM Appendix F) cannot be differentiated from smaller trees, making it impossible to verify clearance compliance for large trees from overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan showing proposed trees

comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan from trees to the overhead electric conductor or poles. Because no dimensions are present, the method of measurement (whether from pole centerline versus conductor, whether from trunk center versus canopy edge) cannot be evaluated. If clearance dimensions were to be added to the plan, they must originate from the outside conductor position, not pole centerline.
applicableAreas: Landscape plan areas where clearance dimensions are or should be shown

comment: No clearance dimensions are shown on the landscape plan. Because dimensions are absent, it cannot be determined whether any dimensions that may exist elsewhere originate from tree trunk centers (correct) or tree canopy edges (incorrect). Proper clearance measurement must originate from tree trunk center (planting location).
applicableAreas: Landscape plan areas where clearance dimensions are or should be shown

comment: While the overhead electric line (OHE) is shown on the landscape plan and tree symbols are present, the plans do not provide sufficient information to verify clearances. Specifically: (1) no dimension lines or distance measurements are provided from trees to the OHE conductor; (2) the tree symbols on the landscape plan are not identified by species (only by functional category: M, SY, PL), so utility-compatibility cannot be assessed; (3) utility pole locations are shown graphically but not dimensioned. The lack of dimensional cross-reference and species identification prevents verification that trees comply with required clearance distances from overhead electric facilities.
applicableAreas: Bottom and east property boundaries where the overhead electric line is located and trees are proposed

comment: Cannot determine whether any trees are proposed within prohibited clearance zones without: (1) species identification with UC status verification against ECM Appendix F, (2) mature height identification to determine if trees are large (40+ feet), (3) clearance dimensions from trees to conductors and equipment. Therefore, it cannot be determined whether Austin Energy written approval is required.
applicableAreas: Anywhere trees are proposed within restricted clearance zones (less than 15 ft from distribution conductor, less than 50 ft from transmission conductor, less than 25 ft for large trees from distribution, less than 10 ft from poles, less than 10 ft from pad-mounts, less than 5 ft from underground equipment, or within transmission easement)
